The total supply stands at $72.5 billion, backed by $72.7 billion in reserves, including $35.6 billion in overnight reverse repos, $25.8 billion in short-term Treasuries, $10.6 billion in deposits at systemically important banks, and $600 million in other bank deposits. PANews, October 17: According to official data, over the seven days ending October 15, Circle issued approximately $10.9 billion in USDC and redeemed approximately $11.4 billion in USDC, resulting in a net reduction of about $500 million in circulation.
The total circulating supply of USDC is $72.5 billion, with reserves totaling approximately $72.7 billion, including $35.6 billion in overnight reverse repurchase agreements on U.S. Treasuries, $25.8 billion in U.S. Treasuries with maturities under three months, $10.6 billion in deposits at systemically important institutions, and $600 million in other bank deposits.

excerpts:
# Circle: Understanding the Company Behind USDC
## What Is Circle? Understanding Circle Internet Group
As of September 18, 2026, approximately $72.9 billion of USDC was in circulation. Circle says USDC is backed by highly liquid cash and cash-equivalent assets, with reserves equal to or greater than the amount of USDC in circulation. Circle also publishes monthly reserve attestations from a Big Four accounting firm.
USDC competes most directly with Tether's USDT. USDT remains the largest stable coin by market capitalization, while USDC has built a significant position among exchanges, financial institutions, payment companies, and other regulated-market participants. As of September 18, 2026, USDT had a market capitalization of about $193.6 billion compared with approximately $72.9 billion for USDC.

...

## How Does Circle Make Money?
The basic mechanism is straightforward. When USDC is issued, Circle holds reserve assets against the tokens in circulation. Those reserves generate interest and other income, while Circle can use part of that income to fund its operations and distribute economics to partners that help expand the USDC ecosystem.
This makes two variables particularly important to Circle's financial results: the amount of USDC in circulation and the income earned on its reserves.

### USDC Reserve Income
Reserve income is the financial engine behind Circle's current business. Circle invests the reserves backing USDC in highly liquid assets, including cash and short-duration U.S. government securities and related instruments. As USDC circulation increases, the amount of reserves generating income also increases. Interest rates therefore matter significantly to Circle.
When short-term interest rates are high, the yield generated by USDC reserves can increase, boosting reserve income. Conversely, falling interest rates can put pressure on revenue even if the amount of USDC in circulation continues to grow.
This creates an important relationship for CRCL investors:
**USDC circulation × reserve yield = a major component of Circle's revenue potential.**

...

## What Drives Circle Stock Price?
**USDC circulation** is one of the most important factors. A larger USDC supply generally means a larger pool of reserves generating income. Circle reported that USDC circulation reached roughly $73 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while its broader strategy continues to target stablecoin adoption across exchanges, financial institutions, payments companies, and other applications.
**Interest rates** are another major factor. Because Circle earns income from USDC reserves, changes in short-term interest rates can affect the amount of revenue generated from a given level of USDC circulation. A growing USDC supply can partially offset lower yields, but the two variables should be considered separately.

...

## Circle Stock Performance
For investors analyzing CRCL's historical performance, it is therefore useful to separate short-term stock-price movements from the underlying operating indicators: USDC circulation, reserve income, distribution costs, interest rates, and growth in Circle's payments and infrastructure businesses.

...

results.title: What Is USDC? How Circle's Stablecoin Works | BIT
excerpts:
# What Is USDC? How Circle's Digital Dollar Works
## Key Points
Backing:** Cash and short-dated US Treasuries, mostly held in a BlackRock-managed government money market fund [4] , with monthly attestations reviewed by Deloitte.
> **4. Size:** About $73.3 billion in circulation at the end of June 2026, and $14.8 trillion in on-chain transfers during the second quarter alone.
> **5. Depeg:** In March 2023, $3.3 billion of reserves was trapped at the failed Silicon Valley Bank. USDC fell to $0.87 before recovering within days.
> **6.
2026:** Circulation dipped from a peak near $80 billion, while Circle launched its own blockchain, Arc, on 16 September with USDC as the currency for network fees.

## What Is USDC?
**USDC** is a fiat-backed stablecoin. For every USDC in circulation, its issuer, **Circle** , holds one US dollar's worth of cash or short-dated US government debt in reserve. Approved customers can hand Circle a dollar and receive one USDC, or hand back one USDC and receive a dollar.

...

## USDC vs USDT
|  | USDC | USDT |
| Issuer | Circle Internet Group (US, NYSE-listed) | Tether Limited (El Salvador-registered, part of the iFinex group) |
| Launched | 2018 | 2014 |
| Share of stablecoins | About 27% (Q2 2026) | The majority |
| Reserves | Cash and short-dated Treasuries, mostly in a BlackRock-managed fund | Mostly Treasuries, plus other assets such as gold, bitcoin and secured loans |
| Reserve reporting | Monthly attestations, daily fund holdings | Quarterly attestations |
| EU MiCA status | Compliant since 2024 | Not compliant; delisted by several EU exchanges |
| Main strongholds | US exchanges, DeFi, payments and institutions | Offshore exchanges, Tron, emerging markets |
| Freezing | Yes | Yes |

...

## How Circle Makes Money
That makes Circle's business highly sensitive to three numbers:
  1. how much USDC is in circulation,
  2. the interest rate it earns on reserves [7] ,
  3. and the share it keeps after paying partners.
The second quarter of 2026 shows how they interact. Average circulation rose 25% on the year to $76.5 billion, but the return on reserves fell by 0.66 percentage points to 3.5% as US interest rates came down. Total revenue reached $701 million, up 7%, and missed analysts' estimates. Distribution and other costs came to $412 million, mostly payments to partners.
In other words, more USDC does not automatically mean more profit for Circle. When rates fall, Circle needs much more USDC in circulation to earn the same income. That is one reason the company is diversifying into payments, blockchain infrastructure and tokens.

...

## Where USDC Stands in 2026
**A slower year for supply.** USDC ended 2025 with $75.3 billion in circulation, up 72% on the year, and Circle has guided for 40% average annual growth over a full market cycle. 2026 has been flatter. Circulation peaked near $80 billion, then slipped from $77 billion at the end of March to $73.3 billion at the end of June. It was still 19% higher than a year earlier, and stood at $73.7 billion in late August.

...

Circle has also created a network token, ARC. It sold $222 million of ARC in a private presale in May 2026, at a $3 billion network valuation, and minted the full 10 billion supply at launch, while stressing that this is not a commitment to list the token publicly. Arc currently runs on proof of authority [14] , and Circle is exploring a move to [proof of stake](https://www.bit.com/knowledge-hub/proof-of-stake-pos) in 2027.

...

## Analogy: The Casino Chip With a Public Vault
Think of USDC as a casino chip worth exactly $1.

...

## Fun Fact
When USDC broke its peg in 2023, it took another stablecoin down with it. DAI, which was designed as a decentralised alternative to company-issued dollars, held more than 3.1 billion USDC as collateral at the time and slid below $1 the same weekend. The episode prompted a lasting debate in DeFi about how "decentralised" a stablecoin can really be when much of its backing is another company's token.

...

## Why It Matters for Investors
USDC is also a useful signal. Growing circulation usually means fresh dollars entering crypto, and shrinking circulation means money leaving. Watch it alongside USDT supply to gauge market liquidity.

...

* KuCoin News via TechFlow, " [USDC Circulation Increases by $1 Billion in 7 Days](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/usdc-circulation-rises-1-billion-in-7-days) ." Circulation, reserves and reserve composition as of 27 August 2026.

...

* Cointelegraph, " [USDC Slowly Repegs on Unconfirmed Reports of SVB Resolution](https://cointelegraph.com/news/usdc-slowly-repegs-on-unconfirmed-reports-of-svb-resolution) ," 11 March 2023. The SVB exposure, the $0.87 low and DAI.
* Fortune, " [Circle Adds Cross River as Banking Partner and Expands BNY Ties](https://www.fortune.com/crypto/2023/03/12/circle-adds-cross-river-as-banking-partner-and-expands-bny-ties-usdc-peg-closes) ," 12 March 2023. How the peg was restored.
